title: Conserving Wildlife through Demand Reduction and Supply Alternatives: Two Experiments in Restaurants in Kinshasa
Irrigation Infrastructure and Satellite-Measured Land Cultivation Impacts: Evidence from the Senegal River Valley
abstract: Expanding irrigation in sub-Saharan Africa is widely viewed as a promising strategy for closing yield gaps and enhancing resilience to climate change. Drawing on more than 3,000 satellite images over a 30-year period, we examine the impact of irrigation infrastructure development in the Senegal River Valley. We find that cultivation rates increase substantially following irrigation project completion. Cultivation rates are remarkably stable at around 25 percentage points above pre-irrigation levels for the first 20 years, and trend even higher from years 20 to 25. Moreover, we show that crops cultivated on irrigated land are significantly less sensitive to both positive and negative temperature shocks, underscoring the role of irrigation in climate adaptation. Despite these aggregate gains, we document considerable heterogeneity in project outcomes, with intermittent land use remaining widespread. To shed light on these patterns, we complement the satellite analysis with farmer survey data, which point to persistent water access constraints as a key barrier to continuous cultivation—constraints that cannot be resolved solely through individual farmer action. • We use over 3000 satellite images to study irrigation infrastructure development. • Cultivation rates increase persistently following irrigation project completion. • Intermittent land use is widespread among irrigation projects. • Farmer survey data point to water access constraints as a barrier to cultivation.
abstract_zh: 在撒哈拉以南非洲扩大灌溉，被广泛视为缩小产量差距并增强气候变化适应能力的一项有前景的战略。利用30年间超过3,000幅卫星影像，我们考察了塞内加尔河谷灌溉基础设施建设的影响。我们发现，灌溉工程竣工后耕种率大幅提高。耕种率在灌溉前水平的基础上，于最初20年间稳定地高出约25个百分点，并在第20至25年间呈进一步上升趋势。此外，我们表明，灌溉土地上种植的作物对正向和负向温度冲击的敏感性均显著降低，突显了灌溉在气候适应中的作用。尽管总体收益可观，我们仍记录到项目结果存在相当大的异质性，间歇性土地利用仍然普遍。为揭示这些规律，我们以农民调查数据补充卫星分析，结果表明，持续存在的用水获取限制是实现持续耕种的一个关键障碍，而这些限制仅靠农民个体的行动无法解决。• 我们使用3,000多幅卫星影像研究灌溉基础设施建设。• 灌溉项目竣工后，耕种率持续上升。• 间歇性土地利用在灌溉项目中普遍存在。• 农民调查数据表明，用水获取限制是耕种的一个障碍。
